items.text:
广州 自家糖水

群友推荐的店面，小小角落一间但味道很不错。糖水我最热爱的就是香芋西米露，这家做得还可以，芋头很香，椰奶也浓厚，我觉得稍微有一点点太甜但是无伤大雅。鱼蛋也好吃，配番茄酱超棒。

抹茶发现 netfilter userspace library "libnftnl" 的 examples/nft-set-elem-add.c 跑不起来，看 syscall 也看不懂，毕竟 netlink msg 谁™能看懂？

一起痛骂 “libnftnl 是什么垃圾” 和 “你的 7.2 内核太新了，新内核全是 bug 很合理” 之后，我也好奇起来了，netlink syscall 报错溯因对我来说也是个谜，正好学习一下，而且这周工作写文档太恶心了想裸奔。

经过一堆准备工作之后：
1. 修改代码让它变成一个“启动暂停、 ctrl-c 继续运行” 的两阶段程序，延长进程生命方便我用 pid 过滤事件
2. 下载 linux-image-$(uname -r)-dbgsym 方便映射符号
3. 准备 @eBPFTalk001 的 bpfsnoop 方便用 lbr 回溯内核执行流
4. 准备 brendangregg/perf-tools 方便用 funcgraph 
5. 下载 Ubuntu-hwe-6.17-6.17.0-35.35_24.04.1 源码
神秘的 Linux 内核系列又回来啦！

首先要找个合适的回溯点。直接从 __x64_sys_sendto syscall 回溯 lbr 得不到太多信息，全是 kfree_skb 之类的清理，所以找找看 netfilter netlink error 相关的 kprobe，结果还真找到一个：
```$ bpftrace -p $(pidof nft-set-elem-add) -e 'k:*nf*err* {printf("%s\n", probe);}' 
Attached 11 probes
kprobe:nfnl_err_add```
然后用 lbr 检查内核是如何执行到这里的：
```$ ./bpfsnoop -k nfnl_err_add --output-lbr --filter-pid $(pidof nft-set-elem-add) --mode entry
      __nla_validate_parse+0xb6  (lib/nlattr.c:655)                    -> __nla_parse+0x23                (lib/nlattr.c:734)                   
      __nla_parse+0x35           (lib/nlattr.c:734)                    -> nft_data_init+0x77              (net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:11894)
      nft_data_init+0xae         (net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:11847) -> nft_data_init+0x115             (net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:11890)
      nft_data_init+0x11a        (net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:11890) -> nft_data_init+0xba              (net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:11912)
      nft_data_init+0xe0         (net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:11912) -> nft_add_set_elem+0x2be          (net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:7380) ```

还有另一种思路，看整个 syscall 的 funcgraph，也能看到 nfnl_err_add 和完整的执行流
```$ ./funcgraph -p $(pidof nft-set-elem-add) -m 50 __x64_sys_sendto
  6)               |              nf_tables_newsetelem [nf_tables]() {
  6)   0.634 us    |                nft_set_lookup_global [nf_tables]();
  6)               |                nft_add_set_elem [nf_tables]() {
  6)   0.586 us    |                  nft_data_init [nf_tables]();
  6)   1.659 us    |                }
  6)   7.547 us    |              }
  6)               |              nfnl_err_add [nfnetlink]() {
  6)               |                __kmalloc_cache_noprof() {
  6)   0.106 us    |                  __cond_resched();
  6)   1.109 us    |                }
  6)   1.444 us    |              }```

两份 trace log 一结合，立刻能知道是在 nft_data_init() 里返回了 -EINVAL，然后用 lbr 跳转记录仔细跟一下源码，看到这一条跳转：
```nft_data_init+0xae (net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:11847) -> nft_data_init+0x115 (net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:11890)```
对应的源码是
```11846         if (desc->len) {
11847                 if (len != desc->len)
11848                         return -EINVAL;
[...]
11890                 return -EINVAL;                                                                                                                                                                                
[...]```
看懂了吧，len != desc->len 所以 return -EINVAL，看下 desc->len 是 nft_set->klen 由 nft table 的 set type 决定的长度，比如我是用
```nft add set ip t s '{ type ipv4_addr; }'```
定义的 ipv4_addr type, desc->len = klen = 4；但是 nft-set-elem-add.c 里传给 netlink 的 uint16_t data 长度是 2，所以内核检查不通过，返回 -EINVAL，QED。

你以为我很高兴吗，不，我很悲伤，因为我其实一开始就用 LLM 解答万物了，把 Linux 源码 + nft-set-elem-add.c 源码 + strace 日志扔给 codex5.5 medium，它只用了三十秒就找到了问题；然后我自己再用上面这些眼花缭乱的 tracing 手段去追溯源码，用了一个小时。投降了，已皈依 LLM 神教饶我狗命🐕

webpage.title: The Scanline Sweeper: A Glyph Rendering Algorithm
webpage.description:
The Scanline Sweeper is an algorithm I developed for the game engine I'm working on. Like other approaches before it, it renders glyphs directly from Bézier curve data on the GPU. Unlike other approaches though, it does so using a continuous coverage estimate, which is more naturally numerically robust compared to computing per-sample winding numbers.

Follow me on bsky: https://bsky.app/profile/scuff3drook.bsky.social

Companion paper: https://rookandpossum.com/posts/scanline-sweeper/

Chapters:

0:00 Scanline Sweeper demo
0:53 Motivation and overview of other techniques
3:50 Scanline Sweeper overview
9:48 Implementation
10:51 Bézier monotonicity demo
13:09 Bézier subdivision demo
15:10 Quadratic Bézier root finding
19:53 Contour overlap handling
20:25 Monotonic intersection code
22:50 Scanline sweep code
27:52 Pixel footprint code
31:18 Half-precision usage
32:42 Higher quality footprints
34:35 Performance evaluation
36:44 Future optimization discussion
39:05 Outro!

Credit to  @SebastianLague  who did a great job covering and tackling the problem space of writing a glyph ray stabber:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SO83KQuuZvg

Understanding how this works isn't needed to understand the scanline sweeper, but you'd need that knowledge to understand how to evaluate the tradeoffs between the two techniques. The SLUG paper was mentioned in the video and likely may have been useful to me, but I confess I read it only after the video was made -- I thought the technique was still patented at the time I made this video and implemented the code.

Tessellation is another technique for rendering fonts aside from texture sampling, SDF sampling, and ray stabbing. I don't cover this because it's not as practical to ship a tessellator for use in a real-time game engine.

Other references consulted:

- https://wdobbie.com/post/gpu-text-rendering-with-vector-textures/
- https://hhoppe.com/ravg.pdf (Random-Access Rendering of General Vector Graphics by Nehab and Hoppe)
- http://rastertragedy.com/
- https://faultlore.com/blah/text-hates-you/

If you're new to the theory of texture filtering in general, I suggest reading Heckbert's thesis: https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/1989/Archive/CSD-89-516.pdf (Fundamentals of Texture Mapping and Image Warping). Excellent must-read document for any graphics programmer IMO (some of the best papers are from this era).

I mentioned in the video something about my use of the mad instruction. I picked up this habit originally from a presentation by Emil Persson: https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1020352/Low-Level-Shader-Optimization-for
Usage on this instruction is also covered in this post: https://momentsingraphics.de/FMA.html

https://momentsingraphics.de/FMA.html

As with all of the content on this channel, NO AI was used to do ANYTHING. No AI to research the code, no AI to implement it, no AI for authoring the script for this video, no AI to edit the video, etc.

If you appreciate this sort of content, consider supporting us at https://www.patreon.com/c/RookAndPossum (totally optional, all educational materials we provide will always be freely available). We are a newer two-person studio, working on a game. I (Rook) am putting special effort into creating educational content along the way, not because this is going to help us get a game out the door faster, but because it's just something I want to do.

If you use any of these ideas in your own work, attribution is certainly appreciated, but not required.
